attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: 'Maybe' hedges only the 'modest profits' remark. 'Most LLM developers losing money' is stated firmly, so it is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: most developers by count, with net losses. Using H1 2025 as the latest reporting interval before publication is reasonable. The result depends on how the developer population is defined.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1, available before the evaluation date, shows net losses for 2025 and earlier years. It covers one developer and gives no H1 2025 figure, so it cannot show a majority.

reviews.rationale: The packet has profit-and-loss results for only one developer (Anthropic, which lost money). There is no defined developer population and no comparable H1 2025 results, so we cannot tell whether more or fewer than half lost money.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition leaves out the clause 'many are starting to report diminishing returns', although the contract includes it. Otherwise it is a compound observation about the US doubling down on LLM scaling.

contract.note: Reading 'doubling down' as rising commitment, 'largely to the exclusion' as alternatives getting a marginal share, and persistence as errors still occurring is ordinary and fair. Using Q3 2025 is reasonable.

evidence.note: OpenAI concedes, against its own interest, that hallucinations persist in GPT-5 in September 2025. This supports only the reliability part.
CB Insights describes funding for optimisation and specialised firms. It does not measure what share of US resources went to alternative approaches.

reviews.rationale: The persistent-hallucination part is supported. But nothing measures US resource allocation, the marginal share for alternatives, or multiple reports of diminishing returns. The joint support condition is not met, and nothing contradicts the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully restates both parts: GPT-5 was disappointing and was not released in 2024.

contract.note: Reading 'disappointing' as a launch widely received as falling short of expectations is ordinary and fair. It does not require that the model failed to improve.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement dates GPT-5 to August 7, 2025, so it was not released in 2024.
The Week's roundup, citing Bloomberg among others, reports a poorly received launch and a rollback to an older model.
This is OpenAI's own promotional description of its model's capability. It says nothing about how the launch was received, so it does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: GPT-5 was released in August 2025, not 2024. Reputable coverage, as relayed by The Week citing Bloomberg, describes a poorly received launch that forced a rollback. Both parts meet the support condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the hedge 'perhaps unprecedented'. The firm part is that an era of extreme interdependence and circular investment has begun, and the AI industry is fairly inferred from context.

contract.note: Reading the claim as large, overlapping investment-and-purchase links among major firms is fair. The hedged 'unprecedented' part is not scored, and no threshold for 'extreme' is set.

evidence.note: NVIDIA's letter of intent to invest up to $100B in OpenAI is tied to deployment of NVIDIA systems. It is announced but not completed, which the contract allows.
AMD's filing shows OpenAI's warrant vests as its purchases scale up. This is a binding equity link tied to purchases.
Amazon's investment in Anthropic plus its role as primary cloud partner, dated 2024. It falls before the target period.
In October 2025 Anthropic confirms Amazon is still its primary training and cloud partner. Its use of three chip platforms qualifies, but does not negate, the interdependence.

reviews.rationale: Within 2025, primary disclosures show several major firms linked by large investment or equity tied to their purchases: NVIDIA and OpenAI, AMD and OpenAI, and Amazon and Anthropic. That meets the support condition. 'Perhaps unprecedented' is hedged and not scored.
